body:
# Independent audit of arbitrary-base upward max propagation

Source: `candidate 23587fb4045280b8`, Sections1--9, including the deficient-rank repair.

Result: PASS. The construction gives exact compatible paths and their
actual first costs; it does not prove a paying menu exists.

1. The anchored coefficient polytopes are finite-dimensional compact
polytopes. Any extreme representation with positive target coefficient
is the self representation. A generic linear height therefore supplies
a strictly higher charged input for every nonself extreme relation.
All propagation paths are finite and acyclic.

2. The transfer supremum uses fixed compact ORIGINAL partner bodies,
so uniform continuity on swept compact sets proves joint continuity.
Physical convexity, monotonicity, and preservation of a finite maximum
all hold with the factors1/lambda retained. Upward induction proves the
least-demand assertion for this particular sufficient system; it does
not imply minimal cost among compatible fields using multiple inputs.

3. The positive inner homothet estimate follows directly from the
uniform speed/support-distance bound and works also at zero speeds.
The selected input alone pays the target field for every actual eroded
input tuple. Original support-function compatibility then proves each
extreme relation exactly. Decomposing a nonextreme coefficient vector
and taking the same original input points proves every remaining
relation by target convexity. Grouping hull points by base verifies
the exact prescribed fibers.

4. My initial audit flagged lower affine-rank bases: their fiber hull
alone has no ambient interior. The source now explicitly supplies
rational orthogonal thickening below the projected-integer-lattice gap.
This creates an ambient convex body while preserving every integer
fiber and every mixed mass. It correctly drops any claim that this
thickening is contained in an originally supplied ambient C. The mixed
sets remain nested, which is what the fixed-cover argument needs.

5. Maxima of finitely many continuous convex fields satisfy the audited
nonsmooth continuum-normal variation theorem. The closed-cap selectors
retain whole fibers on pure-integer boundaries, full inside-support
status, and zero outside-support status. A proper cut has surface-null
boundary intersection. Only a fixed finite menu is used for uniform
little-o control.

6. The projective seed retains its original cost d_i. Incoming demands
can increase the final cost without increasing every cap in the same
proportion; the source correctly does NOT replace d_i by D_(p_i).
Contributions from distinct source fibers add, while coincident-fiber
seeds do not yield additive lower credit automatically.

7. The finite-cover descent test uses the original Q and total M,
actual cap losses and every input cost. Nestedness preserves the cover,
strict gaps preserve slack rows, and the finitely many positive
surpluses provide a common strict decrease. No implicit source
selection or supporting-allocation theorem enters.

8. The exact interval cost2^(m+1)-1 follows from the bound
(j-i)/(q-i)<=1+j-q<=2^(j-q) and the adjacent bracketing relation
attaining equality at each step. The resulting scalar speeds are convex
on the base, so this is an actual exponential-cost calibration. It is
properly distinguished from a universal lower bound for all compatible
continuations.

9. Fiber intersections prove maximum closure for ANY independently
compatible finite arrays, even when produced by different height orders.
This assertion does not commute intersection with hull between integer
bases. The source makes that distinction explicit. The signed min-field
correction in(21) is exact; no sign is silently discarded. Sum-field
compatibility is limited to arrays with the pointwise anchored payment
property, as required.

The companion exact example
`candidate 709f4ee1b13a1688`
now both certifies an actual strict sharing gain and records an actual
case where merging two descent paths erases descent. These calibrations
support the retained signed-payment and menu-selection limitations.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
